questions.question: What happens if you forget to set git user.name and user.email before committing?
choices: Git will refuse to create the commit
Commits will show 'unknown' as the author
Git will use your OS username automatically
The commit will fail silently with no output
questions.explanation: Git doesn't enforce identity configuration. It will create commits, but the author field will show 'unknown', making it impossible to tell who wrote what.

questions.question: In a valid commit chain, what should the first commit's parent be?
choices: The hash of the second commit
questions.explanation: The first commit in a repository (root commit) has parent === null. This is the starting point of the entire commit chain.

questions.question: Why is it important to check that config.name and config.email are non-empty strings (not just truthy)?
choices: Git treats empty strings as valid names
A whitespace-only string like ' ' is truthy but would show as blank author
JavaScript truthy checks are faster than string comparison
It doesn't matter — any truthy value is fine
questions.explanation: A string containing only spaces (' ') is truthy in JavaScript, but would appear as a blank author in git log. You must trim whitespace and check for actual content.
